turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would call Estella at the door, though he felt a bit uneasy about it.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham instructed Pip to call Estella and to wait for her to come.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would wait at the door as instructed, though he felt a bit uneasy about it.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched Pip leave and then called out for Estella, her voice echoing through the silent halls of Satis House.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip waited at the door as instructed, his heart pounding and his hands fidgeting with the hem of his shirt.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched as Pip waited nervously at the door, her eyes filled with a mixture of curiosity and a cold, calculating resolve. She called out to him, her voice cutting through the silence like a knife, asking him to come closer so she could observe him more closely.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt Miss Havisham’s gaze like a cold wind and, though his legs trembled, he took a hesitant step forward.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip to come even closer, her eyes narrowing as she scrutinized him with a mixture of disdain and fascination.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would come closer, his movements slow and deliberate as if each step might trigger some unknown consequence.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham beckoned Pip to stand directly in front of her, her hand outstretched as if to touch him, though her fingers remained hovering in mid-air.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would stand closer, his eyes fixed on her hand as if it were a magnet drawing him in.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to look into her eyes, her voice a mixture of command and melancholic curiosity.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would look into her eyes, though he felt a shiver run down his spine as he did so.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip to describe his life outside her walls, her voice tinged with a curious yet detached interest.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that his life was simple, spent working at the blacksmith's and visiting the church on Sundays.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip about his dreams and aspirations, her voice holding a hint of a question she herself had long forgotten to ask.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he did not have many dreams beyond learning the blacksmith’s trade and maybe one day owning his own forge.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip about his feelings towards the people in his life, her eyes narrowing as if she was searching for something elusive in his responses.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he felt a great deal of affection for his sister and the villagers, even though he sometimes found their rough ways difficult to understand.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he ever felt a sense of longing, her tone distant and almost wistful, as if she was recalling a feeling she had thought long lost.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Pip, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Pip?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip informed Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer; let her look at him. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was not afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched here?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he did, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip what she touched?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that it was broken!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired. She wanted diversion, and she had done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies, and she had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was not, ma’am, he was very sorry for her, and very sorry he could not play just now. If she complained of him he would get into trouble with his sister, so he would do it if he could; but it was so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham remarked that it was so new to him, so old to her; so strange to him, so familiar to her; so melancholy to both of them! She asked Pip to call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to call Estella. At the door.
